options.parentAdvice: Your child needs review of short vowel sounds. Write the word "bot" on a piece of paper. Have your child identify if each letter is a consonant or vowel. Once your child confirms have them write a "c" or a "v" under each letter in bot. Ask your child, to point to the vowel, then ask them does a vowel or consonant come after the vowel in the word. Child should say consonant. When they do, inform them that when they see at least one consonant after one vowel then the vowel will say it's short sound. Have them tell you the short sound. Then have them read the word to you. Practice with the following words: hop, pot, mop.

Your child will need to memorize this word as it does not follow the silent e rule. Your child will expect the o to say its long sound because of the e at the end, but "gone" says the short o sound. Play a game of tic tac toe. Create a 3 by 3 chart and write the word gone in several boxes along with decodable words such as got and hop. You and your child will go back and forth reading a word and marking either an X or O over it. Hint: leave the word 'gone' for your child to mark.

Write oa, oe, and oy on several index cards. Hide the index cards around the house and once your child finds the index cards they make the sound that the letters represent.

Your child will draw an image to help with the /ee/ sound. Have them write the word see on an index card. Draw eyes in the opening of the ee's and say this is the word see and underline ee. Say this part says ee. We draw eyes because we use our eyes to see. You can take the step further and have them draw the temples (long arms on the glasses) to really further the drawing.

Your child needs to learn the three sounds that /ea/ can make. Give your child 3 index cards or divide a piece of paper in thirds write /ea/ at the top and the sound it equals (e.g., ea= E, ea= e, ea= A) Then your child will draw an image on the index card or in the correct column with a key picture that will help them remember all sounds.

Your child needs to learn the two sounds that ie make and when they make them. Teach your child that ie says I when they are the last letters in a one syllable word. ie says E when it is inside or in the middle of a word. Write a few words on index cards and hide them around the room. Have your child look for each word and when they find them ask them to read the word. Ask them what are the two sounds that ie can say and once they answer ask them which sound is in this word and if they need help remind them of the rule.

Create index cards with an OU word on the front. On the back, draw a key symbol (that the child picks as a clue image for them). Front: Youth → Back: drawing of the key symbol. Front: Pound → Back: drawing of the key symbol. Have the child look at the front, try to read it, and flip it over to self-correct. Group the cards they miss into a "try again" pile.

Your child will need to memorize the spelling of this word as the sounds do not follow the rules of phonics. Have your child come up with a mnemonic phrase or help your child. The sillier the better as your child might memorize it better. Suggested sentence: Witches happily ate tacos. The child will work on memorizing the sentence and when they say each word in the sentence the first letter of the word will be how the child spells the word.

Front: Soup → Back: drawing of the key symbol. Front: Moon → Back: drawing of the key symbol. Have the child look at the front, try to read it, and flip it over to self-correct. Group the cards they miss into a "try again" pile.

Your child will need to memorize this word as they cannot decode it. Play a game of tic tac toe. Create a 3 by 3 chart and write the word friend in several boxes along with decodable words such as frog and fresh. You and your child will go back and forth reading a word and marking either an X or O over it. Hint: leave the word 'friend' for your child to mark.

Remind your child of when a short vowel sound is used compared to the long vowel sound. Write the word "fed" on a piece of paper. Have your child identify if each letter is a consonant or vowel. Once your child confirms have them write a "c" or a "v" under each letter in fed. Ask your child to point to the vowel, then ask them does a vowel or consonant come after the vowel in the word. Once they respond with a consonant, remind them that if there is a consonant after a vowel in a one syllable word then the vowel will say its short sound. Have the child read the word. Practice with: Nest, bed, leg
